title: Frozen public feature baseline
acceptance: Every research-report feature, SDK, plugin, configuration family and operation has a stable identifier and source; new documentation changes create a reviewed delta rather than silently changing scope.

title: Commit and artifact provenance
acceptance: Each reused source or binary has a selected release, full commit or immutable digest, origin, license, notices and dependency list; unset pins block implementation qualification.

title: No paid authentication entitlement
acceptance: Start and exercise every built-in capability without an authentication-vendor account, subscription, activation key, usage meter or license-validation service.

title: Restricted material exclusion
acceptance: Dependency and artifact scans find no unapproved enterprise source, enterprise binary or runtime download; proprietary code is neither copied nor used to manufacture fake entitlements.

title: Reproducible source build
acceptance: Build the chosen OSS components and our changes from the recorded sources in a clean environment; compare declared artifact hashes and SBOM contents.

title: No hidden outbound dependency
acceptance: With auth-vendor domains blocked, first-party login, refresh, MFA, administration and local risk evaluation pass; explicitly configured social/mail/SMS traffic is separately allowlisted.

title: Owned configuration and data export
acceptance: Export application, tenant, user, roles, provider references, policy and audit data without a vendor service, then restore into an independently deployed instance.

title: Bounded compatibility claims
acceptance: Publish exact supported core/API/SDK/plugin versions and distinguish functional parity, wire parity, security quality and deployment evidence.

title: Application isolation
acceptance: The same external email can identify unrelated users in two applications, and tokens/data cannot cross the app boundary.

title: Default app and tenant
acceptance: A fresh installation creates the documented default logical application and tenant, and omitted addressing resolves only to those defaults.

title: Tenant-specific identity namespaces
acceptance: The same email, phone or provider account in two tenants may create distinct identities without an application-global uniqueness constraint accidentally merging them.

title: Explicit user sharing
acceptance: Within an allowed shared storage boundary, explicitly associate one app-scoped identity with two tenants while retaining separate tenant sessions and role assignments.

title: Primary and method-specific identities
acceptance: Preserve stable primary IDs and method/recipe IDs, with explicit mappings rather than treating a provider account as the complete application user.

title: Tenant membership lifecycle
acceptance: Add and remove memberships with authorization checks; removal prevents new tenant sessions and invalidates access according to the declared revocation profile.

title: App-level roles and tenant assignments
acceptance: Define a role once per application and assign it differently for the same user in different tenants; verify both positive and forbidden access.

title: App-level user metadata
acceptance: Shared tenant membership does not duplicate or leak the app-scoped metadata record across applications.

title: Separate persistence domains
acceptance: Place selected applications or tenants on separate database deployments and reject identity-sharing operations that cross an unsupported physical boundary.

title: Host and routing resolution
acceptance: Resolve app/tenant from validated host, route and caller configuration; substituting a host header or tenant parameter cannot select another customer's identity context.

title: Provisioning lifecycle
acceptance: Create, configure, list, suspend and delete apps/tenants using idempotent jobs, explicit destructive-operation policy and audit records.

title: Concurrency and uniqueness
acceptance: Simultaneous sign-up, membership change and linking tests preserve all uniqueness and foreign-key invariants without orphaned credentials.

title: Email and password registration/login
acceptance: Correct credentials create/resolve the expected tenant identity; wrong credentials and disabled accounts cannot create authenticated sessions.

title: Username and password
acceptance: Configured username login uses a tenant-scoped normalized identifier without leaking identity existence across tenants.

title: Phone and password
acceptance: Support the documented customized phone/password use case with phone normalization and independent verification state.

title: Custom sign-up/sign-in fields
acceptance: Validate added fields on the server and in UI, return stable field errors and prevent client-side-only policy bypass.

title: Password hashing and rehash
acceptance: Verify supported imported hash fixtures and rehash after successful authentication under a configured modern policy; never expose the hash to clients.

title: Password reset lifecycle
acceptance: Issue, expire and atomically consume a reset token; replay, wrong-tenant and concurrent consumption attempts fail.

title: Registration control
acceptance: Disable open registration while preserving administrator or explicitly invited registration paths.

title: Password-manager behavior
acceptance: Browser autocomplete, generated-password and paste flows work in supported browsers; accessible field labels remain intact.

title: Authentication hooks and overrides
acceptance: Pre/post hooks, API overrides and function overrides receive documented context and cannot implicitly bypass shared authorization invariants.

title: Password change security
acceptance: Require appropriate recent authentication, notify according to policy and apply the declared session-revocation policy after a change.

title: Email OTP
acceptance: Start, deliver, consume and expire email codes; enforce attempt limits, tenant binding and one-time use.

title: SMS OTP
acceptance: Run the same lifecycle through a configurable SMS adapter without an auth-vendor delivery dependency.

title: Magic links
acceptance: Support link creation and consumption with allowed redirects, expiration and replay protection.

title: Combined OTP and link flows
acceptance: Where configured, code and link refer to one controlled pre-authentication flow and cannot produce conflicting identities through concurrent consumption.

title: Resend and throttling
acceptance: A resend observes configured cooldowns and attempt policy; overlapping delivery does not reset brute-force protection or extend validity unexpectedly.

title: Code administration
acceptance: Check, list and revoke one or all active challenges under authorized backend operations without exposing raw secrets to users or logs.

title: Invitation-based sign-up
acceptance: Invitations bind intended app/tenant, recipient and expiration; reuse or recipient substitution is rejected.

title: Allow-list sign-up
acceptance: Apply tenant-specific allow-list rules before creating a user; disallowed recipients receive a non-enumerating error profile.

title: Customization and providers
acceptance: Customize OTP/link templates, verification behavior and hooks; provider failure leaves challenge and delivery state reconcilable.

title: Link-preview safety
acceptance: Mail scanners/prefetch do not silently authenticate or consume high-impact actions; a documented confirmation mechanism preserves supported link flows.

title: Built-in provider catalog
acceptance: Supply integration/configuration paths for Google, Google Workspaces, Apple, Discord, Facebook, GitHub, GitLab, Twitter, LinkedIn, Okta and Active Directory; SAML is tracked under enterprise federation.

title: Custom OAuth/OIDC provider
acceptance: Register a custom provider with validated issuer/endpoints, claim mapping and callback behavior; reject mismatched issuer or audience.

title: Provider client variants
acceptance: Select distinct client configurations by tenant/platform while preventing secret/configuration crossover.

title: Authorization callback integrity
acceptance: Validate state and the applicable nonce/PKCE/issuer binding; duplicate or swapped authorization callbacks do not sign in a different session.

title: Apple callback handling
acceptance: Exercise Apple's documented callback representation and state preservation rather than assuming every provider uses an identical redirect query flow.

title: Claims and email trust
acceptance: Treat provider subject and issuer as identity evidence; an unverified email claim alone never causes privileged linking.

title: Provider invitations and hooks
acceptance: Run invitation, allow-list and customization policies consistently on third-party sign-in and sign-up.

title: Secret and credential rotation
acceptance: Rotate provider secrets/certificates without exposing them to browser bundles or losing tenant configuration rollback.

title: Per-tenant login configuration
acceptance: Configure enabled password, passwordless and enterprise providers separately per tenant and return only allowed login methods.

title: Common-domain tenant discovery
acceptance: Discover/select a tenant through a configured shared login domain without unauthenticated disclosure of sensitive tenant membership.

title: Subdomain login
acceptance: Resolve a tenant from an allowlisted subdomain and prevent host-header or suffix-matching spoofing.

title: Domain ownership and onboarding
acceptance: Verify ownership before granting domain-directed routing, and handle ownership expiry, conflicts and transfer with audit records.

title: SAML service-provider flow
acceptance: Validate signed assertions, issuer, audience, destination, request correlation and validity; reject replay and malformed XML fixtures.

title: SAML metadata and certificate lifecycle
acceptance: Import/export metadata, support planned certificate rotation and reject untrusted endpoint/configuration updates.

title: Legacy SAML migration
acceptance: Convert documented legacy configuration and mapping behavior or supply an explicit tested adapter; do not label an untested metadata import compatible.

title: Tenant provider administration
acceptance: Tenant-authorized administrators can configure their own connections but cannot read another tenant's secrets or edit platform-level providers.

title: Federation mapping and logout
acceptance: Map identities and memberships predictably and document/test the extent of SAML/OIDC logout and local-session invalidation.

title: Authorization code with PKCE
acceptance: Public and confidential clients complete the applicable secure authorization-code flow; code reuse, wrong verifier and redirect substitution fail.

title: Issuer discovery and keys
acceptance: Publish correct issuer metadata and JWKS, with exact issuer/audience verification and key-rotation overlap tests.

title: Client registration and administration
acceptance: Create, list, update, disable and remove OAuth clients; validate redirects, grants and authentication methods per client.

title: Login and consent interactions
acceptance: Expose accept/reject login, consent and logout decisions with one-time request binding and least-privilege scope approval.

title: Shared-backend multi-domain SSO
acceptance: Two frontend domains sharing one backend authenticate via top-level redirects and keep domain/session boundaries intact.

title: Separate-backend multi-domain SSO
acceptance: Two independently configured backend applications reuse central login without sharing raw application refresh tokens or collapsing app identity namespaces.

title: Desktop and native login reuse
acceptance: Use external-browser authorization and validated callback/deep-link handling for desktop and mobile clients.

title: Scopes and custom claims
acceptance: Issue only approved scopes/claims; reserved claims cannot be overridden and unauthorized application roles do not propagate.

title: Userinfo, introspection and revocation
acceptance: Implement authorized userinfo/introspection and token/client revocation with defined propagation and audience restrictions.

title: Logout and session inventory
acceptance: Support local app logout, OAuth-session logout and central SSO logout as separate explicit operations with tested effects.

title: Token lifecycle and consent records
acceptance: Persist grants/consents and apply expiry, rotation and revocation independently from application cookie sessions.

title: Legacy provider behavior
acceptance: Identify required legacy documented token/client behavior and test a migration adapter without enabling prohibited password-grant shortcuts for new clients.

title: Client-credentials grant
acceptance: An authorized service obtains an audience- and scope-restricted token; an end-user credential cannot impersonate a machine client.

title: Service credential management
acceptance: Create, rotate, expire and revoke machine credentials with audit and overlap policy.

title: Service authorization
acceptance: Enforce service-specific permissions and tenant restrictions on every protected operation.

title: Machine token validation
acceptance: Validate issuer, audience, time and scopes on service requests and distinguish service principals from human sessions.

title: Legacy M2M transition
acceptance: Import/migrate documented legacy machine configuration with controlled overlap and removal of old credentials.

title: No volume licensing
acceptance: Issue and validate machine tokens without per-token billing logic or vendor quota enforcement in the software.

title: Protected resource metadata
acceptance: The protected MCP endpoint publishes version-pinned OAuth protected-resource metadata and an authorization-server discovery path.

title: Client authorization flow
acceptance: Run browser authorization and PKCE for supported MCP clients; client metadata/registration requirements are explicitly profiled to the selected protocol version.

title: Resource and audience binding
acceptance: Requests include the required target resource and the MCP server rejects tokens issued for another server or API.

title: Tool-level scope checks
acceptance: Tool invocation receives authenticated identity/context and checks the required scope and application/tenant permission.

title: Authentication errors and challenges
acceptance: Produce the correct authentication challenge and insufficient-scope behavior; no raw bearer token is reflected in errors.

title: No token passthrough
acceptance: Do not forward an inbound bearer token to an unrelated downstream service; obtain an explicitly scoped credential through a supported delegation path.

title: Compatibility sample
acceptance: Ship an independently self-hosted MCP sample that authenticates, invokes an allowed tool, rejects a forbidden tool and handles logout/token expiry.

title: Registration options and credentials
acceptance: Generate challenge/options and verify credential registration with configured RP ID, origin, user-verification and algorithm policy.

title: Passkey sign-up and sign-in
acceptance: Support the documented creation and existing-user authentication flows, including invalid credential and user-not-found outcomes.

title: Credential inventory
acceptance: List, name where supported, and remove credentials without exposing private material or another identity's credential metadata.

title: Challenge lifecycle
acceptance: Expire/remove options and reject duplicate, wrong-origin, wrong-RP and wrong-tenant responses.

title: Account recovery
acceptance: Issue/consume recovery credentials with a strong approved recovery policy, notifications and session revalidation.

title: Passkeys as an MFA factor
acceptance: A verified passkey can satisfy the configured factor/assurance policy without counting one ceremony twice as independent factors.

title: Browser and device coverage
acceptance: Test supported browsers plus real native/device scenarios; virtual authenticators alone do not qualify device compatibility.

title: Migration constraints
acceptance: Preserve RP ID and origin-compatible credentials where possible, otherwise mark required re-enrollment explicitly rather than claiming portable passkeys.

title: Session creation
acceptance: Issue an app/tenant-scoped handle, access token and refresh credential only after required authentication policy succeeds.

title: Local JWT verification
acceptance: Normal protected requests verify cached signing material and claims locally; invalid issuer, audience, algorithm or expired token is rejected.

title: Stateful refresh rotation
acceptance: Atomically compare and rotate server-side refresh verifiers; concurrent refresh and response-loss cases follow a documented tested state machine.

title: Refresh reuse detection
acceptance: Distinguish allowed race/retry behavior from stale-token replay under a versioned policy, and revoke the intended token family on confirmed compromise.

title: Logout and session invalidation
acceptance: Revoke one or all authorized sessions; subsequent refresh fails while existing access-token behavior matches the declared revocation mode.

title: Online revocation mode
acceptance: An explicit denylist/version check enforces a measured bounded revocation window; dependency failure follows a documented security policy.

title: Cookie and header transfer
acceptance: Support both transport modes with correct secure storage, CSRF protections, headers and cookie path/domain flags.

title: Subdomain session sharing
acceptance: Share sessions only across explicitly configured trusted subdomains in the same allowed identity context; tenant switching requires a distinct tenant session.

title: SSR protection
acceptance: Server rendering validates sessions without accidentally refreshing from a browser-only context or leaking tokens into rendered HTML.

title: WebSocket verification
acceptance: Verify initial upgrade and enforce expiration/revocation policy during a long-lived socket; reconnect and reauthentication are tested.

title: Claims and session data
acceptance: Read/update server-side session data and JWT claims with stable regeneration semantics and protection of reserved claims.

title: Signing key modes
acceptance: Support configured static/dynamic signing-key behavior, versioned key rotation and old-token overlap; retired keys expire from acceptance.

title: Anonymous sessions
acceptance: Create limited anonymous sessions and upgrade them without session fixation or unintended role inheritance.

title: Impersonation
acceptance: Require privileged recent authentication, record actor and subject, enforce bounded duration and exclude prohibited actions.

title: Multiple API endpoints
acceptance: Multiple configured resource APIs use the right token audience and shared refresh policy without duplicate refresh storms.

title: Interceptors and explicit mode
acceptance: Fetch/XHR/client integrations support refresh coordination and an opt-out/manual mode with no silently unprotected requests.

title: Error contract
acceptance: Preserve refresh, expired-session, invalid-claim, forbidden and network-failure distinctions expected by supported SDKs.

title: Iframe behavior
acceptance: Document and test behavior with supported third-party-cookie/storage policies; use a supported fallback rather than claiming to bypass browser restrictions.

title: Path and domain migration
acceptance: Changing auth base path/domain has a tested transition policy for cookie scope and old sessions, including safe forced reauthentication when necessary.

title: Server outage behavior
acceptance: Unexpired offline-verifiable access can continue under its profile; new login/refresh and state-dependent checks fail according to documented boundaries.

title: TOTP device enrollment
acceptance: Create, verify, name, list, remove and import TOTP devices; protect secrets at rest and do not activate unverified enrollment.

title: TOTP verification controls
acceptance: Enforce accepted skew/period, failed-attempt policy and replay prevention for relevant operations.

title: Email and SMS second factors
acceptance: Deliver and verify independently scoped OTP challenges with expiry, cooldown, retry policy and tenant binding.

title: Per-user and tenant-wide requirements
acceptance: Require factors for everyone or selected users according to tenant/app policy; removing a factor cannot silently clear mandatory MFA.

title: Factor discovery
acceptance: Return available, enrolled and required factors consistently to backend and frontend clients.

title: Step-up authentication
acceptance: Require appropriate factor class and recent authentication for a sensitive action; a stale MFA claim alone does not satisfy freshness.

title: Recovery codes
acceptance: Generate, display once, hash, rotate and consume recovery codes atomically; reuse is rejected across replicas.

title: Factor independence
acceptance: Passwordless email plus another email challenge is not misrepresented as two independent factors; policies state the achieved assurance.

title: Route and UI enforcement
acceptance: Backend guards enforce verification status regardless of hidden UI controls; prebuilt/custom UI represents enrollment and challenge states.

title: Recovery and factor replacement
acceptance: Require a documented recovery proof, notify the user and re-evaluate active sessions when factors are reset or replaced.

title: Verification status
acceptance: Query verification status for the correct identity/email and distinguish account-level from current-email state.

title: Send and consume verification
acceptance: Send, expire, remove and consume single-use verification tokens with wrong-tenant and replay rejection.

title: Manual administrative actions
acceptance: Mark verified/unverified through privileged audited actions; applications cannot forge the result through profile updates.

title: Protected-route behavior
acceptance: Enforce verification claims on API and UI routes, with bounded stale-claim handling after state changes.

title: Custom and embedded UI
acceptance: Support embedded verification state, resend actions, text/styling and redirect customization.

title: Email change handling
acceptance: Updating an email invalidates or re-evaluates old proof and linking policy without granting trust to the replacement address.

title: Brute-force detection
acceptance: Rate and behavior rules cover login, reset, verification and challenge endpoints, including distributed attempts and tenant/account lockout abuse.

title: Breached-password detection
acceptance: Check against an approved locally available dataset or optional adapter without logging plaintext or transmitting full password hashes.

title: Impossible-travel signal
acceptance: Evaluate time/location uncertainty and VPN/proxy effects; uncertain geography yields an explicit unknown signal, not certain fraud.

title: Bot and credential-stuffing signal
acceptance: Combine request/challenge/velocity evidence; test both scripted attacks and legitimate automation/accessibility cases.

title: Suspicious IP signal
acceptance: Support approved local IP/ASN/Tor/proxy/reputation feeds with version, age and license metadata; no proprietary intelligence endpoint is required.

title: New-device detection
acceptance: Track a scoped, privacy-conscious device recognition signal with reset, loss and cookie-blocking scenarios.

title: Device-count tracking
acceptance: Count observed devices using defined retention and confidence, without treating every cookie reset as a confirmed new human/device.

title: Requester correlation
acceptance: Correlate available requester signals with explicit confidence/limitations; do not promise identification of arbitrarily disguised devices.

title: Risk policy and action contract
acceptance: Return allow, challenge, step-up or deny plus reason codes and policy version; challenge completion is bound to the original transaction.

title: Unknown and outage state
acceptance: Missing or stale signals remain unknown; define minimum local protections and fail-open/fail-closed behavior by action and severity.

title: Risk administration and audit
acceptance: Explain decisions, configure tenant policy, review outcomes and redact sensitive inputs from telemetry.

title: Detection quality evaluation
acceptance: Measure detection and false-positive rates on a documented corpus and lawful available reference tests; never equate an API-shaped stub with comparable protection quality.

title: Self-hosted challenge default
acceptance: Generate and verify local challenges without vendor keys and reject expired/replayed/wrong-site responses.

title: reCAPTCHA v2/v3 adapters
acceptance: Implement documented provider adapters with site/action/hostname validation; use only when operator-configured credentials permit.

title: Turnstile adapter
acceptance: Implement server-side validation and equivalent error mapping without making the service mandatory for core operation.

title: Conditional flow enforcement
acceptance: Apply challenge rules to configured sign-in, sign-up, reset and passwordless flows with consistent server enforcement.

title: UI, accessibility and degraded clients
acceptance: Support suitable accessible challenge/fallback behavior and measure impact on constrained devices; proof-of-work alone is not labeled a complete bot detector.

title: Role and permission lifecycle
acceptance: Create, update, list and delete roles; grant/revoke permissions with stable app scope.

title: Tenant-specific assignments
acceptance: Assign/remove roles to users in a tenant and query users by role and roles by permission without cross-tenant leakage.

title: Backend guards
acceptance: Require authenticated context and enforce role/permission claims at each protected API operation.

title: Frontend guards
acceptance: Provide route/component helpers while documenting that server authorization remains mandatory.

title: Authorization change propagation
acceptance: Removing privileges affects access within the selected online/offline claim freshness contract and refresh regeneration behavior.

title: Resource isolation integration
acceptance: Sample document/database/search endpoints enforce tenant/resource ownership even when the user has a valid platform token.

title: Search and user inventory
acceptance: List, filter, search and paginate users with stable cursor behavior and authorized tenant/application scope.

title: Counts and activity
acceptance: Produce total/active-user counts and administrative statistics using documented definitions without fee enforcement.

title: Profile updates
acceptance: Let users update permitted fields with validation, recent-authentication checks where required and protected fields unavailable to mass assignment.

title: User metadata
acceptance: Get, merge/update and remove app-scoped metadata with size limits, version control and safe reserved namespaces.

title: Deduplication
acceptance: Identify potential duplicates and resolve them through the explicit verified linking workflow, not blind same-email merges.

title: User banning
acceptance: Enforce app/tenant-scoped bans on login, refresh and applicable active sessions; unban behavior is audited.

title: Progressive profiling
acceptance: Require configured fields at defined stages while keeping incomplete profiles from accidentally receiving privileged access.

title: Deletion and retention
acceptance: Delete users and dependent state using explicit retention/legal policy; restore/deletion reconciliation does not resurrect removed access.

title: Primary-user creation checks
acceptance: Determine whether a method identity can become primary without conflicting with another primary identity in the applicable namespace.

title: Link-possibility checks
acceptance: Return deterministic conflict outcomes for already-linked identities and account information conflicts.

title: Manual linking
acceptance: Require proofs of control for the accounts involved and a recent-authentication policy before transactionally linking.

title: Automatic linking policy
acceptance: Enable only for explicit verified/trusted evidence rules; an equal unverified email or broad domain match is insufficient.

title: Add social or password method
acceptance: Attach additional login methods to the intended primary user without changing ownership or bypassing verification requirements.

title: Unlink semantics
acceptance: Preserve valid remaining login paths and defined method-identity lifecycle; prevent accidental last-method lockout.

title: Merge/split transaction integrity
acceptance: Concurrent linking/unlinking preserves unique ownership, tenant membership and credential invariants.

title: Session and authorization consequences
acceptance: Resolve subject/recipe IDs consistently after link/unlink and revoke or regenerate affected sessions without transferring unintended roles.

title: Self-hosted dashboard
acceptance: Serve all dashboard assets and APIs locally with your own branding and no required vendor login.

title: Unlimited licensed administrator count
acceptance: Create, update, list, disable and delete administrators without software seat entitlements; normal capacity and security limits still apply.

title: Administrator authentication and sessions
acceptance: Enforce administrator MFA, list/revoke administrator sessions and separate dashboard credentials/authorization from ordinary users.

title: User operations dashboard
acceptance: Search/edit/delete/ban users, inspect metadata/roles and revoke sessions with authorization, confirmation and audit.

title: Tenant/application management
acceptance: Create/configure apps and tenants, manage membership and login methods, and inspect isolated user pools.

title: Enterprise provider management
acceptance: Configure provider metadata, secrets/certificates and domain ownership with masked secret fields and audited changes.

title: Delegated administration
acceptance: A tenant administrator can manage only delegated resources; platform administrator functions remain inaccessible.

title: Configuration and diagnostics
acceptance: Expose authorized configuration/status/stats with secrets redacted; liveness and database readiness are visibly distinct.

title: Risk and lifecycle workflows
acceptance: Present factor reset, linking conflicts, failed imports and risk events with safe remedial actions.

title: Operator-controlled SMTP
acceptance: Verification, reset, invite and email OTP deliver through configured SMTP with no auth-vendor sender service.

title: Custom email adapter
acceptance: Support a typed delivery interface with template data, locale, recipient, idempotency and categorized errors.

title: SMS/Twilio/custom adapter
acceptance: Support the documented Twilio-style integration and a generic SMS interface without a required provider purchase or claim of cost-free SMS transport.

title: Templates and localization
acceptance: Customize sender, subject, HTML/text, links, language and branding safely; untrusted fields cannot inject headers or unsafe markup.

title: Durable outbox and retries
acceptance: Persist messages atomically with challenge intent, retry bounded failures and prevent uncontrolled duplicate sends or reissuance.

title: Delivery operational controls
acceptance: Apply abuse budgets, monitor bounces/errors where available, protect credentials and never log OTPs, raw links or recovery secrets.

title: Bulk import staging
acceptance: Add/list/count/delete staged imports with idempotent batches, schema validation and per-record error reports.

title: Direct and hash-preserving import
acceptance: Import individual accounts and supported hash types using fixtures proving authentication succeeds and unsupported types are reported.

title: No-hash and lazy migration
acceptance: Provide explicitly secured first-login or password-reset flows for accounts without portable hashes; no fabricated password credential is introduced.

title: External user-ID mapping
acceptance: Create/read/update/remove external ID mappings without breaking stable application IDs or linking ownership.

title: Verification, metadata and roles
acceptance: Reconcile verification state, app metadata, tenant memberships and role/permission assignments with zero unexplained differences.

title: MFA and passkey migration
acceptance: Import transferable TOTP state and eligible passkeys; mark nonportable factor/credential material for re-enrollment.

title: Session migration bridge
acceptance: Validate old sessions through an owned authorized bridge and issue new bounded sessions; never assume unrelated token formats are interchangeable.

title: Rownd transition
acceptance: Provide a tested mapping/configuration path for the research report's Rownd migration use case, with explicit source credential/data prerequisites.

title: Historical MySQL to PostgreSQL
acceptance: Supply a supported conversion/reconciliation path for relevant historical schema snapshots; do not add MySQL as a new production dependency by accident.

title: Cutover and rollback
acceptance: Dry-run migration, canary traffic and rehearse rollback; new writes/factors after cutover have a defined reconciliation policy rather than destructive blind downgrade.

title: Domains and paths
acceptance: Support appName, websiteDomain, apiDomain, websiteBasePath, apiBasePath and gateway-prefix equivalents with validated combinations.

title: Origin and CORS handling
acceptance: Support static/dynamic allowed-origin resolution without wildcard credentialed CORS or untrusted reflected origins.

title: Recipe selection and configuration
acceptance: Enable/disable authentication modules with typed validation; disabled modules do not leave accidentally accessible API routes.

title: Private service authentication
acceptance: Authenticate backend-to-core operations with rotatable scoped keys and private networking; public clients never receive control-plane credentials.

title: Core IP filtering
acceptance: Implement allow/deny caller policies with normalized addresses and trusted proxy handling; forged forwarding headers do not bypass them.

title: TLS and proxy deployment
acceptance: Document/run external TLS termination and internal secure transport appropriate to the network boundary.

title: PostgreSQL configuration
acceptance: Support DSN/discrete settings, schema/table namespace equivalents and tested database connection-pool controls.

title: Session and signing configuration
acceptance: Expose access/refresh lifetimes, signing-key mode/rotation and CSRF/cookie options with safe defaults and explicit migration impact.

title: CLI and environment configuration
acceptance: Bootstrap, validate, inspect version/configuration, migrate and export through documented commands without printing secrets.

title: Secret custody and rotation
acceptance: Use encrypted secret storage/external file or vault adapters; test provider, service, DB and signing-key rotation and recovery access.

title: Single-host deployment
acceptance: Supply production-mode containers, private networks, persistent volumes, TLS, health checks and explicit backup instructions; this profile is not described as highly available.

title: High-availability deployment
acceptance: Support redundant auth nodes and an independently resilient data tier, with exercised node/AZ failure and no single proxy/database masquerading as HA.

title: Gateway and application limits
acceptance: Enforce request, payload and rate limits at appropriate public boundaries and handle retry-after/backoff safely.

title: Readiness and liveness
acceptance: Liveness proves process health; readiness verifies required persistence/dependencies and removes a failed node from traffic.

title: Metrics, traces and logging
acceptance: Export self-hosted observability signals and redact passwords, hashes, OTPs, tokens, provider secrets and sensitive profile data.

title: Backup and recovery
acceptance: Encrypt and restore databases, key material and configuration in a fresh environment; record measured recovery results.

title: Upgrade and compatibility
acceptance: Perform schema-compatible rolling upgrades with old/new SDK fixtures, tested rollback boundaries and pinned images.

title: Security update ownership
acceptance: Track upstream advisories, prioritize relevant fixes and run tests on patched dependencies before publication.

title: Load and capacity evidence
acceptance: Publish benchmark hardware, data size, request mix, failure rates and latency distributions; do not claim unlimited throughput from unlimited licensing.

title: Audit and privacy operations
acceptance: Export security/admin history with access control and retention; enforce deletion and privacy choices in logs, backups and local risk datasets.

title: Dependency outage controls
acceptance: Exercise database, cache, SMTP, provider, DNS and signing-key fetch failures with explicitly documented safe behavior.

title: No certification inheritance
acceptance: Provide audit-evidence artifacts and control mapping; do not label a fork SOC 2 certified or promise a contractual vendor SLA from code alone.

title: Node.js SDK
acceptance: Ship recipe APIs, request adapters, verification, errors, hooks and override behavior for the selected Node versions/frameworks.

title: Python SDK
acceptance: Ship and test FastAPI/ASGI and other frozen-baseline adapters, async lifecycle, verification, errors and configuration without Node-only hidden requirements.

title: Go SDK
acceptance: Ship and test middleware/context/request/response integrations and the selected baseline recipe surface.

title: Vanilla JavaScript SDK
acceptance: Provide framework-independent authentication/session APIs, refresh coordination and explicit network-client integration modes.

title: React SDK
acceptance: Provide UI and state/route helpers, hooks, overrides, theme/localization and recipe-composition behavior.

title: React Native SDK
acceptance: Verify header-token storage/refresh, deep links, concurrent networking and lifecycle/resume behavior in supported native environments.

title: iOS SDK
acceptance: Build and test native integration, secure credential storage, refresh coordination and browser authentication callback behavior.

title: Android SDK
acceptance: Build and test native integration, secure credential storage, refresh coordination and browser authentication callback behavior.

title: Versioned feature matrix
acceptance: Record feature-by-language/platform support rather than assuming every upstream SDK implements every recipe; no required original platform is dropped.

title: Consistent error and context contract
acceptance: SDKs expose normalized documented result types, request context and cancellation/retry semantics while preserving per-version compatibility where promised.

title: Prebuilt and custom authentication UI
acceptance: Provide complete login, sign-up, reset, verification, OTP, MFA, passkey and recovery states plus headless APIs.

title: Embedding and component overrides
acceptance: Embed forms within an application and replace documented components without forking the entire UI.

title: Theme and CSS
acceptance: Customize colors/styles, support the documented shadow-DOM choices and preserve accessible focus/validation behavior.

title: Localization and legal links
acceptance: Configure translations, tenant branding and terms/privacy links without requiring a vendor-hosted asset.

title: Post-login redirects
acceptance: Support application-controlled redirects with server-side allowlisting and consistent continuation after MFA/verification.

title: Function/API hooks and plugin ordering
acceptance: Define before/after/error contracts, asynchronous behavior, ordering, exception propagation and context isolation.

title: Network interceptor extension
acceptance: Intercept the documented request boundaries safely while redacting credentials and preventing hook-caused infinite refresh loops.

title: Cross-version extension tests
acceptance: Compile and execute representative customizations on each supported SDK release so an override signature match is not mistaken for semantic compatibility.

title: CAPTCHA Node and React packages
acceptance: Supply both server and UI counterparts with equivalent configuration and hooks, including a fully local default provider.

title: OpenTelemetry Node package
acceptance: Provide equivalent lifecycle tracing/redaction behavior and allow a self-hosted collector.

title: Profile-base React package
acceptance: Supply the profile container/composition entry points required by dependent profile plugins.

title: Profile-details Node and React packages
acceptance: Enforce server-side field policies and corresponding editable/read-only UI behavior.

title: Progressive-profiling Node and React packages
acceptance: Preserve enrollment/completion gating and server/UI consistency through authentication changes.

title: Tenant-discovery Node and React packages
acceptance: Resolve tenant candidates and user choice with enumeration controls and correct app context.

title: Tenants Node and React packages
acceptance: Support authorized tenant management APIs and corresponding customer-facing UI flows.

title: User-banning Node and React packages
acceptance: Apply ban/unban decisions and UI state consistently, including active-session policy.

title: Plugin package provenance
acceptance: Verify each package license, dependencies, version and extension signatures rather than assuming the monorepo root makes every runtime dependency reusable.

title: Next.js App Router
acceptance: Test auth routes, frontend guards, route handlers, proxy/middleware equivalents and server-component/SSR behavior on the frozen Next.js version.

title: Next.js Pages Router
acceptance: Test API routes, frontend guards and server-side session validation in the Pages Router profile.

title: NestJS
acceptance: Supply middleware/guard/decorator integration and error propagation examples backed by tests.

title: GraphQL
acceptance: Supply context authentication, resolver authorization and subscription/session-expiry handling.

title: Hasura
acceptance: Supply claim/JWT or webhook integration with row/tenant permission fixtures; valid authentication never replaces row authorization.

title: Supabase
acceptance: Supply the documented interoperability path with issuer/claim validation and RLS fixtures rather than asserting generic JWT interchangeability.

title: AWS Lambda
acceptance: Test stateless handler startup, request/response cookies, key caching and session verification under concurrency.

title: AWS AppSync
acceptance: Provide an authorizer/session example with explicit identity propagation and unauthorized subscription tests.

title: Netlify and Vercel
acceptance: Provide deployment examples with supported runtime constraints, proxy paths, headers and cookie behavior; these hosts are integrations, not mandatory hosting choices.

title: Reproducible local examples
acceptance: Every integration has a local/test harness plus clearly identified external credentials/prerequisites for live qualification.

title: FDI operation coverage
acceptance: Implement and test all 49 frozen reference operation entries, including documented legacy variants, with exact method/path/header/cookie/error behavior for the declared profile.

title: CDI operation accounting
acceptance: Account for all 156 entries; implement business/admin equivalents and explicitly classify licensing/telemetry differences without fake vendor-license success.

title: Schema and field behavior
acceptance: Capture request/response schemas, missing/null fields, defaults, error variants and pagination; unknown schema fields remain qualification blockers.

title: Negotiated versions and recipe IDs
acceptance: Enforce supported protocol ranges, recipe identifiers and default app/tenant addressing; unsupported combinations fail clearly.

title: SDK differential corpus
acceptance: Execute representative unmodified upstream SDKs where licensed/compatible and maintained forks otherwise; compare observable state, errors, cookies and hooks.

title: No success stubs
acceptance: A route returning the expected JSON shape without required state changes, audit and security behavior fails parity acceptance.

title: Compatibility exceptions
acceptance: Every deviation is versioned and visible; unapproved functional reductions block full parity, while nonfunctional vendor-license differences are never advertised as exact wire equivalence.

title: Requirement traceability
acceptance: Every requirement links to implementation paths, positive/negative tests, a run artifact and reviewer sign-off before it can become verified.

title: Cross-tenant adversarial corpus
acceptance: Test identity collision, session substitution, provider configuration theft, dashboard privilege escape and resource-data leakage across at least two apps and tenants.

title: Concurrency and crash corpus
acceptance: Test refresh, OTP/reset/recovery consumption, linking, credential updates and key rotation across concurrent replicas and injected crashes.

title: Protocol security corpus
acceptance: Validate OAuth/SAML/WebAuthn/CSRF/CORS protections and malformed or replayed inputs using maintained test tooling where suitable.

title: Migration evidence
acceptance: Run realistic data fixtures, reconciliation and rollback; unexplained missing memberships/factors/sessions block migration acceptance.

title: Independent security review
acceptance: Review custom security-critical code and deployed configuration independently from its author; remediate exploitable critical/high findings before production approval.

title: Accessibility and usability evidence
acceptance: Verify keyboard/screen-reader/error/translation workflows and account-recovery usability across supported interfaces.

title: No-fee runtime qualification
acceptance: Block authentication-vendor egress and prove local capability operation; separate genuine external provider transport prerequisites from auth licensing.

title: Final parity publication
acceptance: Publish functional, protocol, SDK, security-quality and operations scorecards separately; skipped or unknown requirements are not counted as passed.
